Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Leicestershire Police recorded 3,023 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 42.6 per 1,000 residents, the 1st highest rate of Leicester's 21 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (163), drugs (49), vehicle crime (28); the evening/night score by violent crime (299), public order (145), anti social behaviour (110). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Castle safe?

Wandroz currently rates Castle in Leicester as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Leicester during the day and an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Leicester at night. This rating is derived from Leicestershire Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Castle safe at night?

At night, Castle is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Leicester. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Castle a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Castle's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Leicester) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. You can search accommodation already filtered to this specific area using the Booking.com link on this page.

Is there official crime data for Castle?

Yes. Castle's rating is derived from Leicestershire Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk, not an assessment — see the note on this page for the exact figure and the methodology page for full sourcing.
